nodes.content: Design a GPU-sharing runtime that bounds inference latency while reclaiming memory from concurrent, stateful training jobs.
requirements: Under admitted mixed workloads, inference p99 latency stays within 1.2× its isolated baseline.
Training maintains forward progress through memory reclamation without restarting or corrupting optimizer state.

nodes.content: Reserve inference VRAM; admit training only when predicted p99 ≤1.2× baseline, reclaiming VRAM through versioned, step-boundary CPU optimizer-state offload.
How can AdamW moments be offloaded and restored without stale updates or encroaching on inference’s reserved VRAM?
Step-versioned AdamW moment swaps at optimizer barriers prevent stale updates and preserve a 4-GiB inference reserve through 1,000 restart-free steps.
Implement step-versioned AdamW CPU swaps at optimizer barriers; enforce the 4-GiB reserve and verify moment checksums across 1,000 steps.
Run 1,000-step mixed AdamW/inference stress tests with forced offloads, checking versioned updates, moment checksums, 4-GiB reserve, and uninterrupted completion.
Across 1,000 steps, 3 of 200 forced offloads restored stale AdamW moments despite matching versions; optimizer checksums diverged.
To address stale restores despite matching versions, CUDA-event-fenced immutable host snapshots should yield zero checksum mismatches over 200 offloads.
Repeat the 1,000-step AdamW/inference stress test with 200 forced offloads, CUDA-event-fenced immutable snapshots, and per-step optimizer checksums.
The 1,000-step rerun completed without restart; all 200 offloads preserved optimizer checksums, with no stale restores.
Adopt CUDA-event-fenced immutable snapshots for AdamW swaps: they eliminated stale restores observed with version-only swaps across 200 offloads.
Replay 10,000 admitted inference requests with adopted fenced AdamW snapshots; measure p99/baseline ratio and 4-GiB reserve violations.
InferenceReplay-v1 report records isolated and mixed p99 latency, their ratio, 4-GiB reserve violations, and 10,000 request traces.
How should admission account for offload DMA contention when predicting inference p99 under mixed workloads?
Stratify InferenceReplay-v1 traces by offload DMA overlap and PCIe utilization; compare predicted versus observed inference p99 per admission window.
InferenceReplay-v1: below 70% PCIe utilization, DMA-aware admission predicted p99 at 1.17× isolated; observed p99 was 1.18×, with zero reserve violations.
Calibrate a burst-aware admission controller from InferenceReplay-v1 traces, gating training microbatches when projected p99 exceeds 1.2× baseline.
Calibrate burst-aware admission on InferenceReplay-v1, gate microbatches at projected p99 >1.2× baseline, and verify uninterrupted fenced AdamW offloads.
Fit a burst-aware p99 predictor from InferenceReplay-v1 traces using queue depth and DMA overlap; gate training microbatches.
BurstGate-v1 ships a trace-calibrated queue-depth/DMA predictor and microbatch gate at projected inference p99 >1.2× isolated baseline.
Replay 10,000 bursty requests through BurstGate-v1 with fenced AdamW offloads below 70% PCIe; measure p99 ratio, reserve breaches, training steps/checksums.
BurstGate-v1 held p99 to 1.18× isolated, but offload prefetch breached the 4-GiB inference reserve in 3/200 swaps.
Retain BurstGate-v1 and checksum-safe fenced snapshots; defer prefetch until unreserved VRAM covers transfer size, addressing 3/200 reserve breaches.
Add transfer-sized unreserved-VRAM checks before AdamW prefetch; rerun burst admission replay measuring p99, reserve breaches, and optimizer checksums.
Implement transfer-sized VRAM checks before fenced AdamW prefetch; replay 10,000 bursty requests, logging p99, reserve breaches, and checksums.
BurstGate-v2 gates fenced AdamW prefetch on atomically reserved transfer-sized VRAM and records burst-replay p99, reserve breaches, and checksums.
How should inference queue growth and DMA overlap determine when training microbatches are admitted during request bursts?
Deferring microbatches when 50-ms queue-growth/DMA forecasts exceed 1.15× baseline should keep p99 ≤1.2× while admitting ≥90%.
Replay 10,000 bursty requests through BurstGate-v2 with 50-ms forecasts and 1.15× gating; measure p99, microbatch admission, reserve breaches, and checksums.
BurstGate-v2 held p99 at 1.18× baseline with zero reserve breaches, but admitted only 84% of training microbatches.
Add deficit credits and ≤2-ms training slices in forecast-safe windows to improve BurstGate-v2’s 84% admission without relaxing latency safeguards.
Can deficit credits admit ≥90% of training microbatches without queueing inference behind nonpreemptible GPU slices?
Using BurstGate-v2’s 84% admission baseline, replay 10,000 bursty requests with deficit credits and ≤2-ms slices; measure admission and p99.
With deficit credits and ≤2-ms slices, admission rose from 84% to 92%; inference p99 was 1.19× baseline across 10,000 requests.
Across distinct burst profiles, deficit credits with ≤2-ms slices should sustain ≥90% microbatch admission and inference p99 ≤1.2× isolated.
Generate three burst profiles from InferenceReplay-v1; replay deficit-credit ≤2-ms slices, measuring admission, p99 ratio, reserve breaches, and optimizer checksums.
Across three burst profiles, admission was 91–94% and p99 1.17–1.19× isolated; zero reserve breaches or optimizer-checksum mismatches.
Adopt deficit-credit ≤2-ms slices with atomic prefetch reservations: 91–94% admission, p99 ≤1.19×, and no recurrence of prefetch reserve breaches.
Capping each credited training kernel at 2 ms should bound inference GPU head-of-line blocking to 2 ms during 4× bursts.
Instrument the adopted scheduler during 4× bursts; measure kernel runtime and inference head-of-line blocking against the 2-ms cap.
Record maximum CUDA kernel runtime and inference head-of-line blocking during 4× bursts under the adopted ≤2-ms slice scheduler.
BurstBlock-v1 trace lists per-kernel CUDA runtimes and per-request inference head-of-line blocking during 4× bursts.
Analyze BurstBlock-v1 maxima, matching >2-ms inference blocking events to credited kernel runtimes and testing the kernel-cap hypothesis.
BurstBlock-v1 showed 3.1-ms blocking despite ≤2-ms kernels; zero reserve breaches under atomic reservations make reserved-VRAM sharing viable again.
Combine atomic inference-VRAM reservations with single-outstanding-kernel training dispatch and inference-priority streams to prevent cumulative head-of-line blocking.
With atomic VRAM reservations, single-outstanding-kernel dispatch and inference-priority streams should keep 4×-burst p99 ≤1.2× while completing 1,000 checksum-correct training steps.
Benchmark priority streams, single-outstanding-kernel dispatch, and atomic reservations under 4× bursts; compare BurstBlock-v1 blocking, p99, and 1,000-step completion/checksums.
Blocking fell from 3.1 to 1.8 ms, but 4×-burst p99 reached 1.24× isolated; 1,000 training steps remained checksum-correct.
Can priority streams and single-kernel dispatch prevent cumulative inference blocking while atomic reservations protect its VRAM?
Trace 4×-burst queues and DMA; compare FIFO versus priority dispatch with atomic reservations on blocking, p99, and reserve breaches.
Instrument BurstBlock-v1’s 4× bursts under FIFO and priority dispatch; attribute blocking and p99 to queues/DMA, audit reservations and 1,000-step checksums.
Under <70% PCIe admission, priority dispatch yielded 1.18× p99 versus FIFO’s 1.25×; 1,000 steps remained checksum-correct, with zero reserve breaches.
Adopt priority dispatch only below 70% PCIe utilization: unrestricted bursts hit 1.24× p99, while constrained bursts reached 1.18×.
Replay BurstBlock-v1 4× bursts with adopted <70%-PCIe priority dispatch, single-kernel training, and atomic reservations; compare blocking, p99, reserve breaches, checksums.
BurstBlock-v1 replay cut blocking from 3.1 to 1.8 ms; p99 reached 1.18× baseline, with zero reserve breaches and valid checksums.
Ship <70%-PCIe priority dispatch with atomic VRAM reservations and single-kernel training; validated p99 was 1.18× with checksum-safe progress.
Integrate shipped <70%-PCIe priority dispatch, reservations, and single-kernel training; validate p99 ≤1.2× and 1,000 checksum-correct, restart-free steps.
Replay BurstBlock-v1 4× bursts through the integrated runtime; measure inference p99, reserve breaches, and 1,000-step optimizer checksums.
ShareGPU-v1 integrates <70%-PCIe priority dispatch, atomic VRAM reservations, single-kernel training, and fenced AdamW offload; includes BurstBlock-v1 validation logs.
